newsitem.title: GERMANY: BUNDS RESUME DOWNTREND AS TREASURIES LOSE GAINS.
newsitem.headline: BUNDS RESUME DOWNTREND AS TREASURIES LOSE GAINS.

text.p: Bund futures resumed their downward trend on Wednesday after Treasuries faltered in the afternoon and the Bundesbank offered a strict warning on interest rates.
At 1516 GMT, the DTB Bund future was down 33 basis points at 101.91, reversing what had been strong gains on Tuesday and raising fears of further declines.
German debt had appeared to be headed higher after U.S. data in the early afternoon, but gains were capped as traders unwound long positions taken near 102.20.
Traders said the market is growing ever more nervous about possible U.S. interest rate hikes and future moves will be closely tied to U.S. data including U.S. consumer prices at 1230 GMT on Thursday.
"The market is moving from number to number and now we are waiting for the U.S. consumer prices," one trader said.

The Bundesbank contributed to the market's unease, saying in its August monthly report it was scrutinising a recent upturn in inflation and would not hesitate to tighten its policy if warranted. "It cannot be overlooked that there has been a stronger rise in consumer prices in the last few months."
The Bundesbank's remarks contributed to a further flattening of the yield curve with the short end of the market underperforming.
The spread between two- and 10-year maturies stood at 182 basis points in late trade.

Analysts said they fear that further declines may be in store for Bunds with speculation mounting that Germany may tighten monetary policy in coming months and Treausries also looking vulnerable to signs of a stronger U.S. economy.
Some said they saw support for the contract at around 101.50 with minor resistance at Wednesday's low of 101.70.
The benchmark cash 10-year Bund was down to 102.29 from 102.48 to yield 5.69 percent.
